acceptance: Every comment in the changed code is one of the four forms — a pointer, a directive, a doc block on an export, a member of one or the module itself, or a comment another house standard requires — and no fifth kind is written.

A doc block on an export, on a member of one — an interface field, an enum case, a class property — or on the module itself, is at most three lines of eighty characters and states what it is, not why it is that way. A tag block such as `@example` below the prose is kept as written.
A reason the user asked to put in a comment is redirected to an ADR, a decision log or a mechanism page, with a pointer left in the code — or dropped.
A test comment that narrates what a case pins is replaced by a better test title, not shortened.
The rule is applied in the language the file is in, using that language's comment delimiters and export keyword from the syntax table.

A comment another house standard requires — a test standard's Setup/Exercise/Verify markers, its axis walk, its named-constant note, its boundary note — is kept, and that standard is read before any comment in a file it governs is cut.
